items.title: Restricted-Gaussian fiber log ratio and exact relative score

source.anchor: Lemma 2 proof, equation (11), used by SPHMC arXiv:2609.06906v1 Lemma 4.17
source.attribution: Yin Tat Lee, Ruoqi Shen and Kevin Tian; used by Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang. ASTIS expanded representative-level proof; no author endorsement implied.

items.statement: For normalized restricted-Gaussian fibers, the canonical log-likelihood ratio agrees almost everywhere under the left fiber with the explicit normalized quadratic exponent difference. For eta>0 the displayed smooth representative has the constant spatial gradient eta^{-1}(y-y'). This is the score calculation in the cited contraction proof, not the contraction itself.
assumptions: The canonical llr identity uses a sigma-finite common base, a measurable left exponent and integrability of both exponential weights.
The source fiber uses eta>0; the reusable calculus theorem only requires eta nonzero.
Almost-everywhere value equality is not converted into differentiability of the canonical measurable representative.

obligations.label: Identify the explicit normalized tilt ratio a.e. with the canonical llr
Prove the exact constant gradient of the displayed smooth representative

bindings.boundary: A.e. value identification under the left tilt only; no classical gradient equality for the canonical llr.

assumption_deltas.source: The two normalized restricted-Gaussian laws are manipulated without an explicit RN representative domain.
assumption_deltas.lean: Sigma-finite common base, measurable left exponent and integrability of both exponential weights.
assumption_deltas.reason: These conditions justify the normalized tilts and Mathlib's canonical llr identities.

assumption_deltas.source: The score is used under the left fiber.
assumption_deltas.lean: Equality is explicitly almost everywhere under the left tilted law.
assumption_deltas.reason: This is the measure required by FI(left||right).

bindings.boundary: Exact equation (11) gradient for the explicit smooth representative only. Canonical-Fisher identification, LSI, T2 and W2 contraction remain open.

assumption_deltas.lean: eta!=0 in a complete real inner-product space.
assumption_deltas.reason: The derivative calculation only divides by eta; the source consumer specializes to eta>0.

assumption_deltas.source: The paper differentiates the displayed log-density ratio.
assumption_deltas.lean: Only the explicitly displayed smooth representative is differentiated.
assumption_deltas.reason: An arbitrary canonical measurable RN representative may change on a null set, so a.e. equality of values does not determine a classical derivative.
